title: When can a lithium-ion cell design search trust a reduced battery model (SPMe) instead of the full DFN model?
lede: research programme on fidelity-aware Li-ion electrode design; milestone 2: on 128 fresh Sobol designs a 10-cycle DFN run ranks designs by 100-cycle DFN energy at Spearman 0.96 against 0.64 for a 100-cycle SPMe run at the same cost (3.6 s vs 3.7 s), replicating 2a's 0.977 vs 0.834 on 49, and the plain SPM beats SPMe (0.96); milestone 1: SPMe's own minimum salt concentration flags the designs it mis-scores (AUC 0.997 on 49, 0.994 on 128) (modelled, PyBaMM OKane2022, stack level)
summary: A research programme (proposal and log on the project page) on when a lithium-ion electrode design search can trust a reduced electrochemical model. Milestone 2 (dense benchmark) runs 128 fresh space-filling (Sobol) designs for 100 cycles under SPM, SPMe and DFN (384 runs, every cycle kept): a 10-cycle DFN run ranks the designs by their 100-cycle DFN Wh/kg at Spearman 0.962 (95% 0.932–0.977), against 0.641 (0.480–0.789) for a full 100-cycle SPMe run, at the same wall time (3.6 s against 3.7 s), and its top 10 contain the DFN-best design, which SPMe ranks 41st. Unplanned: the plain SPM ranks better than SPMe (0.955; 0.984 against 0.769 over the 121 designs SPMe completes), though it over-scores the best design by 20 Wh/kg, and 15 of 128 designs (12%) are mis-scored by SPMe by over 25%. Milestone 2a, the same question on the 49 stratified designs of energy-cell-dfn: 10-cycle DFN 0.977 against 0.834 for 100-cycle SPMe (paired bootstrap difference 0.138, 95% 0.057–0.271), and a linear fade extrapolation fails (Spearman 0.01). Milestone 1: a 2-cycle SPMe run's minimum electrolyte concentration classifies the designs SPMe under-scores by more than 25% with ROC AUC 0.997 on the 49 (0.994 on the 128, whole-run minimum). Re-runs reproduce the committed SPMe and DFN scores exactly. Limits: one parameter set and protocol, costs timed on one design and one 4-core machine, no measured cell for these designs.
